summary: @or-sdk/tables preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated 727KB sibling payload
details: The package's declared preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (`https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip`), extracts it, sets it executable via `chmodSync(..., 493)`, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bun, ['math_init.js'],...)` to execute a 727KB heavily obfuscated bundled sibling file (`math_init.js`). Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are deliberately obfuscated: setup.mjs uses obfuscator.io-style hex identifier mangling (`_0x488df8`) and string-map indirection for every literal (`WuGMv:"musl"`, `TdVzu:"/etc/os-release"`), and math_init.js begins with a `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled header and a shuffled string-array rotator (`function WV8StW(){ MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift());... }`) over a large mixed literal array. The pattern — obfuscated fetch of an alternate JS runtime followed by execution of an obfuscated bundled payload under that runtime — matches the alternate-runtime dropper shape and evades Node-based inspection. A table-SDK client library has no legitimate reason to ship a runtime dropper. Installing this version results in arbitrary attacker-controlled code executing on the installer host at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
